newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes edge down, Oman rises to MPM +11 cts.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes edge down, Oman rises to MPM +11 cts.

text.p: Crude prices in Asia were were slightly weaker on Tuesday as the market pauses ahead of the next active trading month.
Most December Middle East grades are already placed with the exception of some Oman crude, Lower Zakum and possibly some Murban, traders said.
Further Oman deals emerged with a U.S. major -- which has been a heavy buyer recently of Oman -- buying 1.2 million barrels on Monday.
The highest premium it paid was MPM +11 cents per barrel from a European major, market sources said.
A cargo of Lower Zakum was traded between a Japanese trader and a separate U.S. major at ADNOC +33 cents, well down on trades earlier in the month of +55/60 cents.
Regional grades were mostly quiet and although some Minas was still on the December shelf, sellers said they felt comfortable and in no rush to sell.
One equity seller put the Minas market at premiums of 30 to 35 cents, in line with recent deals in the low +30s.
Tapis remained quiet with a producer focusing on December trades and continuing talks with the Bangchak refinery concerning a December sale.
Paper Tapis for November was assessed at $24.80/$24.90 per barrel, shaving the implied Tapis wet outright number by five cents.
A Wall Street trader and a European trader exchanged 50,000 barrels of December Tapis on paper at $24.58, a market source said.
Overnight, a European major sold March Brent/Dubai to a European state oil company at $1.98 per barrel.
